00207.label: First cetuximab dose

medicines.name: Chlorphenamine
medicines.note: NCCP suggested premedication.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.note: NCCP suggested mandatory infusion premedication; reconcile low-risk antiemetic support to avoid duplicate steroid.

medicines.name: Rescue antiemetic
medicines.note: Low emetic risk; use current NCCP/local guidance and account for the infusion steroid.

additional_support: Skin care and sun protection under local EGFR policy.

Monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months after last dose.

00328.label: Day 1 · chemotherapy and antibody

medicines.name: Antihistamine
medicines.dose: As prescribed in the local cetuximab premedication plan
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Repeat for subsequent cetuximab infusions; assess prior infusion reactions.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 8 mg PO once, subject to reconciliation with the cetuximab premedication prescription
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab on Day 1
medicines.note: This corticosteroid also covers the treatment-day corticosteroid part of antiemesis where appropriate. Pharmacy must reconcile route, dose and timing; do not automatically add a second 8 mg antiemetic dose.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: NCIS V8 moderate-risk row; consider QT risk, low electrolytes, interactions and the individual prescription.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: Days 2 and 3 after the administered Day 1 chemotherapy
medicines.note: NCIS V8 delayed prophylaxis. Reconcile with any other steroid prescription; re-anchor dates if treatment is delayed.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.timing: Rescue nausea treatment only as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS V8 rescue option; check contraindications, renal function, interactions and prescribed duration.

medicines.name: Atropine sulphate
medicines.timing: Before irinotecan when prescribed; assess acute cholinergic symptoms
medicines.note: Avoid in glaucoma. Use with caution in asthma; review suitability before prescribing. This treats/prevents the acute cholinergic syndrome; it is not the delayed-diarrhoea rescue medicine.

additional_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
Cetuximab premedication and infusion observation remain necessary even on an antibody-only day.
Start local EGFR skin care; monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before and periodically during therapy, then monthly for two months after the final dose.

Provide a written irinotecan delayed-diarrhoea rescue and escalation plan before treatment; distinguish it from immediate infusion-related cramps/sweating. Fever, severe pain, dehydration or diarrhoea not responding to the prescribed plan needs urgent review.
Confirm line care, pump contact details and disconnection arrangements; report chest pain, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or pump/line problems urgently.

NCCP p1 permits cessation of observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas Erbitux SmPC section 4.2 requires monitoring during and for at least one hour after each infusion. Reconcile and document the local observation plan; do not promise early discharge.
Folinic acid follows the bolus 5-FU hold/omission. Reconcile DPD inhibitors, DPD status and suspected fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity before administration.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide

additional_support: Cetuximab only: no irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil or atropine is scheduled on Day 8.
Continue skin care, electrolyte monitoring, infusion precautions and the urgent contact plan.

Cold exposure can precipitate oxaliplatin neurotoxicity; do not recommend ice chips during fluorouracil in this combination. Review neuropathy every two cycles and sooner if symptoms interfere with function.

If treatment is delayed for cytopenia, follow the source-specific weekly blood-count checks and maximum delay; assess the antibody and chemotherapy components separately when indicated.
EMA Erbitux section4.2: chemotherapy must not begin earlier than one hour after the end of cetuximab.

Medication review: NCCP contraindicates concomitant brivudine, sorivudine and analogues with fluorouracil; review DPD-affecting medicines, phenytoin toxicity/levels and warfarin INR.

00456.label: Day 1 · Cisplatin + etoposide

medicines.name: Aprepitant
medicines.dose: 125 mg orally on the platinum day;80 mg on the next2 days

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: Adjust for QT/individual risk.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 12 mg orally on the platinum day;8 mg daily on the next3 days
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and any other steroids.

medicines.name: Olanzapine
medicines.dose: 5 mg orally on the platinum day and next3 days
medicines.note: Sedation, metabolic risk and other medicines require review.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally three times daily as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS high-risk row has no end-day orPRN qualifier. Confirm duration; coadministration with olanzapine increases extrapyramidal risk.

additional_support: Multiday SACT: reconcile antiemetics for each day’s medicines and the two days after; one combined prescription is required. Do not add independent overlapping courses.
The5-day cisplatin aprepitant extension is not automatically applicable: this regimen gives cisplatin only on Days 1 and 8.
Coordinate radiation-related nausea, swallowing, nutrition, skin care and respiratory assessment with radiation oncology.
No automatic routine G-CSF, antibacterial, antiviral or PJP prophylaxis is specified in these NCCP regimens; consider individual risk and local policy.
Review etoposide interactions, live vaccines, nephrotoxic/ototoxic medicines and any duplicate QT-prolonging antiemetics.

Cisplatin pre/post hydration and electrolytes per local policy. NCCP suggests posthydration10 mmol magnesium sulphate plus20 mmol potassium chloride in 1 L sodium chloride0.9% over2 hours; adjust to patient and local policy.

Day 1 etoposide in 1 L may be considered prehydration; Day 8 has no etoposide infusion, so prescribe its own prehydration. Routine furosemide to induce urine flow is not recommended without fluid overload.
NCCP reduced count rows still require reconciliation with the etoposide SmPC. Count rows apply to etoposide and do not clear cisplatin independently.

After grade 3 non-haematological toxicity (excluding mucositis/alopecia), wait for recovery to grade 1 or less; the source 75% restart requires dose-history and denominator review. Grade 4 is outside that source row.

After grade ≥2 neuropathy recovers to ≤1, a consultant chooses carboplatin AUC5 substitution or 50% cisplatin. Do not restore full-dose cisplatin automatically or substitute the separate AUC3 regimen.
